workingStoryBrief.briefText:
# Working Story

## Pursuit posture
- Buyer: Ridgeview Property Group
- Opportunity: Ridgeview Portfolio Janitorial Services
- Pursuit call: pursue
- Unifying concept: Clean switch, tighter control
- Next checkpoint: Red Review (Evaluator View)

## Opening angle
Ridgeview Property Group should feel less janitorial drag during the day: executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms stay reset, supplies stay stocked, and the property team stops chasing basics.

- Drivers: 4-site portfolio; 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM occupied-hours pattern; Executive floors and lobby touchpoints set the tone; Restocking misses trigger emails fast
- Solution frame: Lead with named day-porter zones, midday reset standards, restroom checks, and same-day supervisor escalation.
- Proof thread: Prove it with 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program and 99.1% stocked restroom compliance in Consumables reliability playbook.
- Close: This variant makes daytime control and management relief the buying reason.

## Reinforce these themes
- Keep occupied spaces inspection-ready: executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms should look reset, stocked, and inspection-ready in the middle of the day, not after an email. Boss Key puts named day-porter zones, response standards, and supervisor escalation behind that promise, backed by 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests, demonstrated in Executive-floor response program. Proof: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program.
- Switch cleanly, improve quickly: Ridgeview Property Group should not spend the first 28 days babysitting a janitorial changeover. Boss Key locks the roster, clears access and equipment before day one, and runs buyer-visible launch huddles, backed by 97% staffing readiness by day 10, demonstrated in Corporate campus mobilization. Proof: 97% staffing readiness by day 10 in Corporate campus mobilization.
- Protect value before talking rate: If Ridgeview Property Group presses on rate, Boss Key can defend the number in operating terms: fewer daytime misses, a cleaner launch, and less tenant emails and property-team chase. That value story is backed by 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints, demonstrated in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.

## Carry this proof
- Executive-floor response program: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests. It directly supports Visible daytime support and Self-performed accountability. Use: Executive-floor theme proof.
- Corporate campus mobilization: 97% staffing readiness by day 10. It directly supports Low-disruption transition and Self-performed accountability. Use: Executive summary opening proof.
- Budget rebaseline without visible slippage: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints. It directly supports Value without service erosion and Floor care recovery. Use: Executive summary value variant.

## Ghost carefully
- Ghost generic daytime coverage: Most bids list day porter hours and call it coverage. Boss Key shows how executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms get reset, stocked, and escalated before the buyer asks twice. Counter with Treat day porter coverage as a customer-facing response layer with named zones and visible standards, not a spare labor bucket. Proof: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program.
- Ghost low-rate instability: A thin rate is not a savings story if it creates more tenant emails and property-team chase, service noise, and launch friction. Counter with Explain how Boss Key protects value by removing avoidable service noise and management overhead before defending the rate. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.

## Transition emphasis
- Occupied-hours assurance: Best when executive floors, lobbies, and high-traffic spaces matter as much as after-hours production.
- Stand up named day porter coverage before steady-state routines begin.
- Use launch huddles to review visible misses and same-day corrective action.
- Give the buyer a simple occupied-hours issue-closure cadence during the first month.

## Answer if challenged
- If your price is not the lowest, what am I really buying?: Show the buyer where the labor and supervision sit: staffed daytime response, floor-care recovery, and a launch plan that does not dump work back on the property team. Tie the number to less tenant emails and property-team chase. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.
- How do I know the first month will not get messy?: Walk through the locked roster, access checks, equipment staging, and weekly launch huddles so the buyer can see who owns day one through day 30. Proof: 97% staffing readiness by day 10 in Corporate campus mobilization.

## Before Red Review (Evaluator View)
- Confirm buyer priorities and proceed with the current pursuit plan.
- Prepare evaluator review packet
- Draft value bridge for rate-sensitive buyer questions

conceptSheet.memoText:
# Working Story

## Pursuit posture
- Buyer: Ridgeview Property Group
- Opportunity: Ridgeview Portfolio Janitorial Services
- Pursuit call: pursue
- Unifying concept: Clean switch, tighter control
- Next checkpoint: Red Review (Evaluator View)

## Opening angle
Ridgeview Property Group should feel less janitorial drag during the day: executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms stay reset, supplies stay stocked, and the property team stops chasing basics.

- Drivers: 4-site portfolio; 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM occupied-hours pattern; Executive floors and lobby touchpoints set the tone; Restocking misses trigger emails fast
- Solution frame: Lead with named day-porter zones, midday reset standards, restroom checks, and same-day supervisor escalation.
- Proof thread: Prove it with 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program and 99.1% stocked restroom compliance in Consumables reliability playbook.
- Close: This variant makes daytime control and management relief the buying reason.

## Reinforce these themes
- Keep occupied spaces inspection-ready: executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms should look reset, stocked, and inspection-ready in the middle of the day, not after an email. Boss Key puts named day-porter zones, response standards, and supervisor escalation behind that promise, backed by 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests, demonstrated in Executive-floor response program. Proof: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program.
- Switch cleanly, improve quickly: Ridgeview Property Group should not spend the first 28 days babysitting a janitorial changeover. Boss Key locks the roster, clears access and equipment before day one, and runs buyer-visible launch huddles, backed by 97% staffing readiness by day 10, demonstrated in Corporate campus mobilization. Proof: 97% staffing readiness by day 10 in Corporate campus mobilization.
- Protect value before talking rate: If Ridgeview Property Group presses on rate, Boss Key can defend the number in operating terms: fewer daytime misses, a cleaner launch, and less tenant emails and property-team chase. That value story is backed by 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints, demonstrated in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.

## Carry this proof
- Executive-floor response program: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests. It directly supports Visible daytime support and Self-performed accountability. Use: Executive-floor theme proof.
- Corporate campus mobilization: 97% staffing readiness by day 10. It directly supports Low-disruption transition and Self-performed accountability. Use: Executive summary opening proof.
- Budget rebaseline without visible slippage: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints. It directly supports Value without service erosion and Floor care recovery. Use: Executive summary value variant.

## Ghost carefully
- Ghost generic daytime coverage: Most bids list day porter hours and call it coverage. Boss Key shows how executive floors, lobby touchpoints, and restrooms get reset, stocked, and escalated before the buyer asks twice. Counter with Treat day porter coverage as a customer-facing response layer with named zones and visible standards, not a spare labor bucket. Proof: 95% same-shift closure on daytime service requests in Executive-floor response program.
- Ghost low-rate instability: A thin rate is not a savings story if it creates more tenant emails and property-team chase, service noise, and launch friction. Counter with Explain how Boss Key protects value by removing avoidable service noise and management overhead before defending the rate. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.

## Transition emphasis
- Occupied-hours assurance: Best when executive floors, lobbies, and high-traffic spaces matter as much as after-hours production.
- Stand up named day porter coverage before steady-state routines begin.
- Use launch huddles to review visible misses and same-day corrective action.
- Give the buyer a simple occupied-hours issue-closure cadence during the first month.

## Answer if challenged
- If your price is not the lowest, what am I really buying?: Show the buyer where the labor and supervision sit: staffed daytime response, floor-care recovery, and a launch plan that does not dump work back on the property team. Tie the number to less tenant emails and property-team chase. Proof: 9% annual operating-cost reduction with no increase in service complaints in Budget rebaseline without visible slippage.
- How do I know the first month will not get messy?: Walk through the locked roster, access checks, equipment staging, and weekly launch huddles so the buyer can see who owns day one through day 30. Proof: 97% staffing readiness by day 10 in Corporate campus mobilization.

## Before Red Review (Evaluator View)
- Confirm buyer priorities and proceed with the current pursuit plan.
- Prepare evaluator review packet
- Draft value bridge for rate-sensitive buyer questions

## Operator notes
Make the buyer picture a calmer property team by day three: executive areas reset, restrooms stocked, launch questions answered, and no one debating who owns the issue.
